description: Coffee to water ratios for pour-over, French press, drip, AeroPress, moka pot, Chemex, V60, and Turkish coffee, plus espresso to milk for lattes and cappuccinos.
intro: Every brew method has its own ratio, and the ratio is the difference between a cup that tastes balanced and one that tastes sour or bitter. Pour-over starts at 1:16. French press starts at 1:15. AeroPress starts at 1:13. The numbers look close, but a step either way changes the cup.

The anchor for all of them is the Specialty Coffee Association's Golden Cup standard: 55 grams of coffee per litre of water, about 1:18, brewed at 92 to 96 C. It was set for drip coffee, and most methods brew a little stronger than that, but it is the reference every ratio below is measured against.

Each calculator below is for one method, with its own starting ratio, water temperature, and brew time. Type the coffee to get the water, or the water to get the coffee, and the answer updates as you type. The table underneath shows the common serving sizes, and the worked example shows the maths.
